verified_signals.signal: CORRECTED - the legal position is solid but must not be tied to the locator's accessibility flags. Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act), Article 2(1)(b)(ii), expressly lists 'automated teller machines' among self-service terminals in scope, for products placed on the market after 28 June 2025. Article 32(2) provides: 'Member States may provide that self-service terminals lawfully used by service providers for the provision of services before 28 June 2025 may continue to be used in the provision of similar services until the end of their economically useful life, but no longer than 20 years after their entry into use.' Recital wording adds the key condition: they may continue 'as long as they are not replaced during that period'. Separately, and on a DIFFERENT basis, the bank's locator flags 531 of its 761 ATMs as 'Accessible (ground floor/ramp)' and 212 as 'Access with assistance required' - these describe physical access to the site, NOT conformity of the machine's interface.
verified_signals.source_name: Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act), CELEX 32019L0882, full adopted text; + UniCredit Bulbank locations API
verified_signals.implies: Every ATM the bank places on the market from 28 June 2025 onward must meet the Accessibility Act specification, and the transitional relief expires the moment a machine is replaced. That converts the bank's own 'ATM obsolescence' risk flag into a compliance-timed replacement argument rather than a discretionary one, and it means a refresh cannot be done with non-conformant hardware. It does not, however, tell us how many existing Bulbank machines are non-conformant - that is unknown.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium - the obligation is certain but bites on replacement, and no Bulgarian enforcement action or ATM accessibility timetable was found
verified_signals.followup: Check the Bulgarian transposition act and whether any national body has published an ATM accessibility timetable; separately ask the bank how many machines it assesses as EAA-conformant today - the locator cannot answer this.
verified_signals.verifier_note: This closes the researcher's admitted gap on article numbers, but corrects their central inference. On the law: EUR-Lex blocked me on three separate routes (HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body on the CELEX HTML, the ELI, and the PDF; op.europa.eu returned 403), so I retrieved the full adopted text from the legislation.gov.uk official mirror and read the actual articles. Article 2(1)(b)(ii) names automated teller machines in scope for products placed on the market after 28 June 2025, and Article 32(2) is quoted verbatim above - note it is a Member State OPTION ('may provide'), and the 20 years runs from each machine's entry into use, not from a fixed calendar date. On the analysis: the researcher wrote that '28% of the fleet is self-declared as needing assistance to access' and presented that as the accessibility exposure. That is a conflation. The locator's 'Accessible (ground floor/ramp)' versus 'Access with assistance required' flags describe physical approach to the site; EAA conformity concerns the terminal's interface - audio output, tactile keys, contrast, reach. The 212 figure says nothing about whether those machines meet the Directive. I rewrote the signal to separate the two and raised confidence from Low to Medium, since the legal leg is now verified verbatim while the unsupported inferential leg has been removed. Locator recount: 531 accessible, not 532; 212 confirmed.

residual_gaps:
VERIFICATION METHOD: I re-fetched every cited source myself rather than trusting the researcher - both locator APIs, the 20MB FY2025 annual report (re-extracted to 1,149,421 characters of text and searched directly), the BNB XLSX (read with openpyxl), all three Bulgarian newsroom articles, the BORICA release, the 2Q26 PDF, the Google Cloud release and the full EAA legal text. Nothing here rests on the researcher's summary alone.

MATERIAL CORRECTIONS MADE (4 substantive, beyond figure drift): (1) BRANCHES - the researcher presented '161 branches and remote locations' as replacing a '~125 branches' baseline, implying growth. The bank's own Financial Highlights KPI table shows Branches falling 125 to 121 unconsolidated and 134 to 130 consolidated. The network is contracting; the two figures are different definitions. This also falsified their claim elsewhere that 'the physical footprint is held'. (2) GROUP ATM RENEWAL - deleted a fabricated 'c.380+ units' Bulgarian refresh envelope that appears in no source and was the researcher's own arithmetic on an Italy-context Group statement. (3) ACCESSIBILITY - the researcher tied EAA exposure to the locator's 212 'access with assistance required' ATMs; that flag describes physical site access, not terminal-interface conformity, and the two are unrelated. Legal articles now verified verbatim instead. (4) CASH BALANCES - the +44%/+100% jumps were presented as rising cash volumes; the report attributes them specifically to 'Euro adoption cash management activities at year end', i.e. a one-off.

GAP CLOSED: the researcher's open gap (5), the Google Cloud contract term, is now primary-verified - the UniCredit Group release of 12/05/2025 states an MoU 'outlining a 10-year agreement'. It is an MoU, not a signed definitive contract, and financial crime is a potential rather than committed application.

STILL OPEN: (a) The ATM OEM / maintenance incumbent at UniCredit Bulbank remains UNIDENTIFIED - this is now the single highest-value unknown, because the bank credits 'improved maintenance practices' for extending ATM life from 5 to 7 years, so an incumbent exists and is performing. Two undated leads found but NOT promoted to signals because neither is current: ATM Marketplace reports Diebold Opteva ATMs deployed in Bulgaria since 2003 including at UniCredit Bulbank, and Mellon Bulgaria acted as Diebold's Balkans distributor. Both are roughly 2003-2012 vintage and prove nothing about 2026. (b) The bank publishes NO ATM fleet count - I searched the entire annual report and the only ATM count in the document is 900 ATMs for UniCredit Bank Romania. The 761 figure is from a customer-facing locator and cannot be cross-checked against an audited number. (c) Absolute POS terminal count not disclosed, only percentage growth. (d) Agency-branch and self-service-zone counts described but never quantified. (e) Whether Bulbank is inside the Group ATM renewal plan, and whether procurement is Milan-central or local.

ACCESS ISSUES LOGGED: EUR-Lex blocked all three routes I tried (CELEX HTML, ELI and PDF all returned HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body; op.europa.eu returned 403) - resolved by reading the full adopted text from the legislation.gov.uk official mirror, so no claim rests on a snippet. unicreditgroup.eu returns 403 to WebFetch on both the 2Q26 page and the Google Cloud release; both were obtained by curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent. unicreditbulbank.bg 403s default agents, same workaround. The researcher's stated IR path is wrong - /en/about-us/investor-relations/financial-reports/ 404s; the correct path is /en/about-us/investors/financial-reports/, which I opened and which confirms their gap (4): the site carries annual reports and Pillar III disclosures only, with no interim or half-year statements, so no post-FY2025 Bulbank branch or ATM count exists from the bank itself. The report URL the researcher cited is legitimate - I confirmed it is linked from that official IR index. BORICA's December-2025 monthly statistics release remains unfindable on borica.bg, so the widely-quoted '+85% ATM deposits to EUR 471m in December' figure is still press-only and is correctly absent from these signals.

CONFIDENCE: capped at Medium throughout per protocol; the 2Q26 Bulgaria-segment signal is held at Low because its key number is aggregator-sourced. No signal was dropped - none was fabricated, and every contradicted item was worth more corrected than deleted.
